generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: A delivery can reconcile stale documentation after code changes yet still miss the inverse failure: newly authored normative documentation may promote desired or planned behavior to current state while executable behavior remains legacy, partial, or absent.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: Treat the newest canonical text as authoritative and validate only old claims against changed code, never testing new current-state claims against the executable candidate.
generalized_learning.prevention_rule: For every new or changed normative current-state claim, the delivery process must identify the executable source and record whether the behavior is current, future, partial, legacy, or absent before accepting the text.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: Independent review must attempt to refute every new or changed normative claim against the frozen executable candidate, not only search for stale older claims.

transfer_cases.procedure: State that a scalar endpoint now partitions totals while the executable handler still returns one scalar; require rejection unless the text marks the capability as future or limited.
State that a feature is enabled by default while executable configuration remains disabled by default; require documentation-claim-drift.
Mark a planned capability as implemented while the executable boundary lacks the behavior; require exact executable parity before accepting the status.

skill_changes.change: Documentation semantic-drift prevention is bidirectional and requires executable_claim_check for new or changed normative claims.
Independent audit detection checks new or changed normative documentation against executable frozen behavior even without a code change.
